A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Super-Linear. Their complete main texts and appendices, including figures, tables, equations, and algorithms, support reliable matching and comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original zero-shot and full-shot forecasting results, inference timings, and ablations on LTSF and GIFT-Eval.

after.justification: V3 retains these original results and adds experiments removing training resampling and excluding overlapping pretraining datasets.

M1.justification: The frequency-specialized linear experts, spectral top-k routing, two-stage training, resampling procedure, and autoregressive forecasting remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 is retained; the stronger emphasis on input adaptation does not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: The new no-leak variant excludes Saugeen, Births, and KDD from pretraining, creating limited variation in training coverage (H.1). Evaluation datasets and tasks remain unchanged. Solar's removal from the pretraining inventory is explicitly described as correcting an erroneous listing.

E2.justification: V3 substantially expands the evaluated comparisons: Chronos-2 appears in Figures 1 and 5 and Table 3; DUET and FEDformer join the full-shot comparison in Table 4; and new Table 7 compares TimeCMA, Time-VLM, and Time-LLM. Existing comparators are retained.

E3.justification: V3 introduces controlled training conditions without resampling and without overlapping pretraining datasets. The existing experiments retain their splits, metrics, training lookback of 512, native forecast horizon of 96, and hyperparameter configurations.

E4.justification: New analyses test dependence on training resampling (Tables 2 and 10) and the effect of pretraining–evaluation overlap (H.1, Tables 17–18). Figure 13 adds comparative forecast case studies across six datasets. These substantially extend the existing component, frequency-selection, and lookback analyses.

E5.justification: The three-seed full-shot reporting and standard deviations in v2 Table 8 are retained in v3 Table 9. The added controls introduce no new seed-count disclosures, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Matched original benchmark scores remain unchanged, but substantial results are added for the new comparators and controls. Without training resampling, LTSF MSE is 0.423 versus 0.265 and GIFT-Eval MASE is 1.603 versus 0.857. The no-leak variant reports 0.863 MASE. These are additional experimental conditions, not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C retain the error bounds, periodicity assumptions, and derivations. New Appendix B.11 interprets the existing bounds and resampling equations in discussing limitations; it introduces no new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion newly emphasize input adaptation and claim that data construction can matter more than architectural modifications. This refines the contribution's emphasis while retaining the central claims of efficient, competitive, interpretable forecasting with linear experts.

C2.justification: V3 adds specific limitations concerning interpolation smoothing, spectral information loss, short-context observability, and autoregressive error accumulation (B.11). H.1 qualifies the zero-shot evaluation through overlap disclosure and interpretation of the exclusion control. The ablation discussion also shifts the principal performance attribution toward resampling.

D1.justification: V3 corrects the pretraining inventory by removing Solar and explains that it was never used, identifies the datasets shared with GIFT-Eval, and specifies their exclusion in the additional model. Hardware, hyperparameter tables, and the implementation-access URL are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: V3 adds citations to DUET, Time-LLM, Time-VLM, and TimeCMA, expands Appendix E's model descriptions, and discusses parameter efficiency and model selection relative to LLM/VLM forecasters in B.4. The main related-work narrative and central research positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: There are targeted edits to the abstract, introduction, ablation discussion, and conclusion, plus new appendix subsections and limited reordering. Terminology, cross-references, and publication headers are updated, while most existing prose and the overall document structure are preserved.

P2.justification: V3 adds the comparative forecast grid in Figure 13 and new comparison/control Tables 7, 17, and 18. It also expands the full-shot and ablation tables and updates Figures 1 and 5 with Chronos-2. These substantially expand the displayed evidence; existing architecture and analysis figures are retained.

improvement.justification: V3 addresses an important validity gap in the zero-shot evaluation by explicitly identifying overlap and testing a model trained without it, obtaining GIFT-Eval MASE of 0.863 versus 0.857. The resampling ablation establishes a major source of performance, while B.11 explains concrete applicability limits. Together these substantially strengthen validation and interpretation, although uncertainty for the new controls remains unreported.
